summary: Ecuador has one of the most open visa policies in the world: almost every nationality enters visa-free for up to 90 days within a 12-month period, with only a short negative list, including Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cuba, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, Syria, Venezuela and, since the 2024 suspension of its waiver, China — needing a consular visa. Andean Community citizens travel on a national ID card.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from or have transited a country with risk of transmission. Vaccination is separately recommended before traveling to the Amazon provinces (Orellana, Sucumbíos, Napo, Pastaza, Morona Santiago, Zamora Chinchipe) and is not needed for Quito, the Galápagos or the highlands.

travelInsurance.text: Ecuadorian law requires foreign visitors to hold health insurance valid for the duration of their stay. Enforcement at mainland airports is inconsistent, but the requirement is real and is checked more often for Galápagos travelers. Carry a printed policy showing medical coverage and dates.

source.name: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Movilidad Humana del Ecuador

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed onward or return ticket is expected and is checked by airlines at check-in.

proofOfFunds.text: Officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for the stay. A bank statement or credit card is normally enough. No fixed amount is published for visa-free visitors, while visa applicants must document economic solvency.

declarations.text: Everyone flying to the Galápagos must register at the Galápagos Governing Council desk in Quito or Guayaquil, pay the transit control card fee and have their luggage inspected for biological material before check-in. Keep the card. It is collected when you leave the islands.

notes: Strict biosecurity applies to the Galápagos: no fresh food, seeds, plants or animal products may be carried to the islands, and bags are screened before departure from the mainland.
Exporting pre-Columbian artefacts or protected wildlife products — including some shell and coral souvenirs — is prohibited.
Drone use requires authorization in national parks and is heavily restricted in the Galápagos.

currency.name: United States dollar (Ecuador has been dollarised since 2000)

payments.text: Ecuador uses the US dollar, so there is nothing to change. Cards work in Quito, Cuenca, Guayaquil and Galápagos hotels, but cash rules in markets, buses and small towns, and almost nobody can break a USD 50 or 100 note, so bring small bills.

safety.text: Ecuador's security situation deteriorated sharply from 2023, with gang violence, states of emergency and periodic curfews concentrated in the coastal provinces — Guayaquil, Esmeraldas, Manabí, Los Ríos and Durán — and along the northern border with Colombia. Quito, Cuenca, Baños, the Andes and the Galápagos remain far calmer, but check current advice and avoid the affected areas.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Ecuador Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: June to September is the dry season in the highlands, best for Quito, Cotopaxi and the Quilotoa loop. The Galápagos works all year — cooler, choppier seas from June to November and warmer, calmer water from December to May.

idp.text: Ecuador is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: The Galápagos has its own charges on top of your flight: the USD 20 transit control card on the mainland and the national park entrance fee, which was raised to USD 200 for most foreign adults in August 2024. Both are payable in cash. Budget for them separately.

The visa-free allowance is 90 days within any 12-month period, not per entry. Leaving and returning does not reset it. A further 90 days must be applied for as an extension, and overstaying triggers a fine and a possible re-entry ban.

Health insurance valid for your whole stay is a legal entry requirement in Ecuador. Checks are patchy on the mainland but more common for Galápagos travel. Carry a printed policy in English or Spanish showing medical coverage and dates.
Quito sits at about 2,850 m and Cotopaxi far higher. Take the first day slowly, and remember the equatorial sun burns fast at altitude even when the air feels cool.

Security in the coastal provinces and along the Colombian border has been volatile since 2023, with states of emergency and curfews imposed at short notice. Travel between cities by day, use registered taxis or apps, and check local news before changing plans.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ecuador?
faq.answer: Almost certainly not. Ecuador waives visas for nearly every nationality, giving up to 90 days within a 12-month period. The exceptions are a short list of nationalities that need a consular visa, including Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cuba, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iraq, Libya, Myanmar, Nigeria, North Korea, Pakistan, Senegal, Somalia, Sri Lanka, Syria, Venezuela and Yemen, plus China since Ecuador suspended the Chinese waiver in 2024. The list has changed several times, so confirm before booking.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Ecuador?
faq.answer: Ninety days within any 12-month period. That allowance is cumulative across all your visits in the year, so a border run does not reset it. An extension of up to a further 90 days can be applied for through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, for a fee, before your current permission expires.

faq.question: What do I need to visit the Galápagos?
faq.answer: No separate visa — the Galápagos is part of Ecuador — but there are extra steps. Register at the Galápagos Governing Council desk in Quito or Guayaquil airport and buy the USD 20 transit control card before check-in, have your bag screened for food and plant material, and pay the national park entrance fee on arrival, which is USD 200 for most foreign adults. You also need a return ticket, confirmed accommodation or a tour booking, and valid health insurance.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Ecuador?
faq.answer: Yes, in law. Ecuador's human mobility legislation requires foreign visitors to hold health insurance covering their stay. Enforcement varies — many mainland arrivals are never asked — but Galápagos operators and some airlines do check, and it is not worth arriving without it.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens still enter Ecuador visa-free?
faq.answer: No. Ecuador suspended its visa waiver for Chinese citizens in mid-2024 in response to irregular migration through the country, and the suspension has remained in place. Chinese passport holders should apply for a tourist visa at an Ecuadorian consulate and confirm the current position, as this policy is under periodic review.

faq.question: What currency is used in Ecuador?
faq.answer: The US dollar — Ecuador dollarised in 2000 and uses US notes alongside Ecuadorian coins of the same value. Bring plenty of small denominations; USD 50 and 100 notes are frequently refused outside big hotels.
